**Meridian Tidal Pilot - Summary**

The sole significant equipment failure was Turbine T-4, taken offline on 14 March 2025 when its bearing seal corroded through, allowing seawater into the nacelle. The root cause was traced to corrosion of the bearing seal housing. Over the 24-month pilot, 18.7 GWh was delivered to the grid, 6 percent below the 19.9 GWh forecast. Final project cost reached EUR 41.25 million against an approved budget of EUR 36.7 million — an overrun of EUR 4.55 million (12.4 percent), driven mainly by the T-4 repair campaign. Environmentally, the independent fish-monitoring programme found no statistically significant change in fish migration counts before and after installation (p = 0.41). Lead engineer Dr. Ines Marchetti recommended replacing the titanium fastener set with duplex stainless steel on all remaining nacelles; this was accepted in principle by the steering group. The final decision: the steering group approved Phase 2 for the third quarter of 2026, contingent on a completed bearing seal redesign and a successful dry-dock endurance test.
